title: llm-kv-prefetch-and-routing-prd-scratchpad-aisha-khan
content: Context / problem - Observed: tail latency spikes for some chat sessions where repeated short turns cause repeated KV cache misses and re-decoding of prefixes. - Separate ideas have been discussed: KV prefetch (user-level or session-level), smarter routing to pinned model variants, and adaptive TTL for cached entries. Need to explore a combined feature: prefetch + routing heuristics to reduce p99 latency without ballooning token cost. Goals - Reduce p95/p99 token-latency for interactive chat workloads by improving KV hit-rate. - Avoid large increases in overall token compute cost (target <10% overhead). - Keep operational complexity manageable (configurable knobs per-customer). Non-goals - Not trying to redesign whole caching subsystem; incremental feature on top of existing KV cache. - Not doing model re-training or prompt-rewriting. High-level proposal 1) Prefetch controller (session-scoped):    - For long-running chat sessions, after user turn N, compute a small set of likely next-prefix tokens / KV entries to prefetch into GPU memory.    - Heuristic sources: previous turns, recent user intent tags, common reply templates (from evals), or lightweight next-token LM (small quantized model) run on CPU.    - Prefetch async with low priority; can be throttled by customer-configured budget. 2) Routing policy awareness:    - Combine prefetch with smart routing: if a session is latency-sensitive, route to lower-quantized/high-memory model variant or to a dedicated pool that keeps larger KV caches resident.    - On prefetch miss or heavy contention, fallback to a compatible variant with warm cache or increase priority for that session's requests. 3) Adaptive TTL and eviction hints:    - Track per-session access patterns and adapt TTL for entries to keep frequently re-used prefixes for longer.    - Eviction hints can be communicated to runtime to avoid evicting session-hot entries during GC. User stories (rough) - As an app developer, I want 99th percentile latency for chat replies to be stable (<300ms extra per turn) even under bursty user typing, so users don't experience stalls. - As an SRE, I want the ability to set per-customer prefetch budgets and priorities to avoid noisy neighbors. - As a product manager, I want to measure cost/latency tradeoffs and be able to roll back prefetch per-customer if cost exceeds threshold. Acceptance criteria / metrics - p95 and p99 token-latency reduction for test workload X (interactive chat benchmark) by at least 20% relative to baseline without prefetch, for small-medium sessions (5-30 turns). - Average token compute overhead across customers <10% (configurable threshold). - No increase in overall error rate (time-outs, OOMs) attributable to prefetch. - Feature gated behind customer opt-in and rollout flags. Design considerations / tradeoffs - Heuristic complexity vs cost: a cheap CPU-side next-token predictor might give reasonable prefetch targets without heavy GPU cycles. But mismatches produce wasted prefetching. - Memory residency: prefetch increases GPU memory pressure. Need eviction hints and per-node budgeting. - Routing coupling: routing to dedicated pools reduces misses but increases cost. Need fallbacks and auto-fallback policies. Implementation sketch (phases) Phase 0: experiment / metric baseline - Build synthetic chat workload harness (based on real traces) to measure baseline KV hit-rate and latency distribution. - Tag sample sessions by turn-count, user-type, prompt length. Phase 1: naive prefetch PoC (CPU predictor heuristic) - Implement simple predictor: repeat last user turn prefix + top-5 likely response-start tokens (from small LM or learned ngram model). - Async prefetch API: runtime endpoint to request loading of KV entries for a session (best-effort). - Measure hit-rate improvement and cost overhead. Phase 2: routing integration + adaptive TTL - If PoC looks promising, add routing tags (latency-sensitive) and per-customer budget controls. - Implement adaptive TTL controller to increase lifetime of hot session entries. Phase 3: smarter predictor & rollout - Replace heuristic with lightweight learned predictor; allow opt-in per customer. - Add console UI: budget sliders, metrics panel (prefetch hits, wasted prefetch tokens, cost delta). Open questions / risks - How to quantify wasted prefetch vs user-perceived latency improvement? Need clear metrics and dashboards. - Security/privilege: prefetching implies loading KV entries for other users/sessions — ensure ACL model respected. - Cost model: how do we attribute GPU memory and compute cost for prefetch to customers? Could be tricky for multi-tenant pools. - Interaction with quantized models: prefetching KV into quantized runtime — any compatibility concerns? Data needed / experiments - Sample chat traces (anonymized) to understand common next-turn patterns. (ask PM/DS for a dataset) - Baseline KV hit-rate per session length. - Cost analysis: token compute delta per prefetch candidate. Rollout plan (high-level) - Canary: internal + 3 low-volume customers opt-in. Monitor hit-rate, p95/p99, cost. - If stable, expand to more customers with graduated budgets. - Add console controls and default for new customers. Next steps / TODOs - [ ] Get anonymized chat traces from DS team (owner: Raja) - [ ] Build synthetic harness and baselines (owner: Aisha) - [ ] Implement async prefetch API stub in runtime (owner: eng infra) - [ ] Quick POA for ACL checks and cost attribution (owner: Emma) - [ ] Draft short RFC for eng review (owner: Aisha) Notes to self - Keep this lightweight; aim for measurable wins first. - Keep per-customer budget/opt-in to reduce blast radius. - Consider pairing with Optimize team to surface suggestion heuristics in console. Fragment ideas (brain-dump) - Use embeddings of last user message to lookup similar past replies and prefetch their KV prefixes. - If a session is using function-calling heavily, prefetch typical tool-call response prefixes. - Cache hint TTL tied to time-since-last-user-typing event (websocket keepalive). References / links - Confluence: KV Cache Notes (linked above). - Jira: JIRA-1345 (prefetch experiment ticket). End of scratchpad.
